habitat: Pairs or groups, sometimes with many young, in woodland and wooded grassland in the east and in thornveld or grassland in the more arid west. Wild birds occur in isolated pockets, especially in large reserves.
summary: A common resident. An enormous flightless bird. The immature is like a small, scruffy female and is usually with adults. The adult male's tail varies from whitish to grey or cinnamon-brown; the identification line says buff, grey or white. The male utters a lion-like roar. The Kemp name Ostrich and the code RB were left unchanged.

calls.description: The male utters a lion-like roar. The grade A recordings from South Africa are ND. The highest-ranked playable file is a grade A gurgle from Texas. A playable grade B call from Limpopo was not selected because the Texas file is a higher grade. The filename is XC845920-Vibrato1_(200701_0762).mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The size is given as 2 m and stored as 200 cm. The male tail is not one colour, and the female plumage is not described beyond the immature comparison. The South African grade A recordings are ND. The selected file is from Texas. A grade B call from Limpopo exists. The iNaturalist account has no display name, so the login sowadart is credited. The Kemp name Ostrich and the code RB were left unchanged.
